patients.summary: Student with beta-thalassemia trait (promoter-region HBB variant) found on a 2019 fatigue workup, a 2022 marathon-associated hyponatremia ED stay, 2025 preconception genetics with her beta-zero carrier husband, and a 2025-26 pregnancy on empiric OB iron. Last seen 2026-04-03 at about 30 weeks; delivered in June 2026, known only by her message.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 20 y/o student starting her third year at a nearby university, wants a primary care doctor close to her apartment. Has the student health insurance plan, card info taken. Prior care was a pediatric office back home; she will sign a release so we can request those records. Scheduled new patient visit 8/22 at 9:40. Membership info and portal invite emailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, low MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

20 year old woman, undergraduate, here to set up primary care now that she lives in the area year-round. No complaints today. Says she has been healthy; saw a pediatrician growing up, no hospital stays, no operations.

Meds: one multivitamin a day, over the counter.
Allergies: none to medications.

Family: Dad has been told he carries beta-thalassemia trait. His mother (pt's paternal grandmother) had beta-thalassemia major. Thalassemia runs in her father's Thai relatives. She has never been tested herself, as far as she knows.

Social: Full-time student, lives with a roommate. Never smoked. Does not drink. Runs a few times a week.

ROS: Negative for fever, weight change, chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, abdominal pain, bowel change, urinary symptoms, rashes. Periods regular, not heavy.

Exam: Well-appearing, pleasant. BP and weight per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without pallor or rash. No edema.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Health maintenance, healthy young adult. Childhood vaccines reportedly complete; will request old records. Flu shot this fall. Cervical screening starts at 21, plan at next physical.
2. Family history of thalassemia. Mentioned that she may carry the trait; no testing today, will revisit if any symptoms or when she is thinking about a family.

RTC for physical next summer.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, left after 15 minutes.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

21F, finished spring semester, staying local for a summer job on campus. Feels well. No new history since last August.

Meds: multivitamin daily. NKDA.
LMP 2 weeks ago, cycles regular. Sexually active with one partner, uses condoms.
No tobacco or alcohol.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet, normal. General well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap obtained. Skin normal. Mood bright.

PHQ-2 0.

Plan:
- Pap today (first screen).
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees.
- Flu vaccine in the fall.
- Old pediatric records still not received; she will ask her mother for her vaccine card.
- Physical yearly.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maricel, your Pap came back normal and your HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Next Pap would be due in three years. Enjoy the summer.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu shot given IM R deltoid, lot and expiration in the immunization record. No contraindications. Pt waited 15 min, no reaction.

reports.text: Test: beta-globin (HBB) gene sequencing including promoter and flanking regions, with deletion/duplication analysis. Indication: microcytosis with elevated HbA2; family history of beta-thalassemia. Result: one heterozygous pathogenic variant identified in the HBB promoter region. Variants of this type lower transcription of the affected allele and are classed as beta-plus alleles. No second HBB variant and no large deletion detected.
reports.conclusion: Heterozygous for a promoter-region beta-plus HBB variant, consistent with beta-thalassemia trait (carrier). Genetic counseling is recommended for reproductive planning; partner carrier testing advised.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired lately

S: 22 y/o, end of semester. A few weeks of feeling a bit run down, mild, still running and getting through classes. Sleeping 6-7 h. No fever, weight loss, night sweats, cough, palpitations. Periods monthly, normal flow. Eats meat and vegetables, no restrictive diet. Mood fine, stress about finals.
Meds: multivitamin. NKDA.
FHx: father beta-thal trait; paternal grandmother beta-thal major; more thalassemia among her dad's Thai relatives.
Never smoker, no EtOH.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable, not pale. No scleral icterus. Thyroid normal. No cervical adenopathy. Heart without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no spleen or liver edge felt. No edema.
In-office CBC result later today: Hgb 11.0, MCV 68.

A/P:
1. Mild fatigue with mild microcytic anemia. MCV is very low for so slight an anemia, and with her family history a thalassemia trait is the leading thought. Sent hemoglobin electrophoresis and beta-globin gene analysis (insurance prior auth started for the gene test). TSH with today's draw.
2. Sleep, finals stress likely contributing. Will call with results; no iron for now.

documents.title: Hemoglobin electrophoresis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Electrophoresis: HbA2 5.4% (high), HbF 2.3% (mildly high), no abnormal hemoglobin bands. With Hgb 11.0 and MCV 68 this fits beta-thalassemia trait. TSH normal. Added to problem list. Gene analysis still pending. Pt messaged.

documents.title: Your blood tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maricel, your thyroid test was normal. The hemoglobin test shows the pattern of beta-thalassemia trait (also called thalassemia minor), the same carrier state your dad has. It usually causes only a mild, lifelong anemia and small red cells, and it does not need iron or other treatment. The gene test should be back in a few weeks and will confirm it. Happy to talk by phone if you want.

documents.title: HBB gene analysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: HBB analysis: heterozygous promoter-region variant, beta-plus allele. Confirms beta-thal minor. Lab recommends counseling for reproductive planning. Will note for the future.

documents.title: Gene test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your gene test confirms that you carry one changed copy of the beta-globin gene. The kind you have reduces, rather than stops, production from that copy. Nothing to do for your own health. The one time it matters is if you plan a pregnancy someday: a partner would want to be tested, and we would send you both to genetics first. I've noted it in your chart.

documents.title: RE: Gene test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you for explaining. Should I still take my multivitamin? And does this mean I should not run? I signed up for a 10k in the fall.

documents.title: RE: Gene test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, the multivitamin is fine. Running is fine too, the trait does not limit exercise for most people. Good luck in the race.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza vaccine IM left arm. Afebrile, no allergy to vaccine components. Observed 15 minutes, fine. Reminded her that her annual physical is overdue; she will book over winter break.
